01.actor: A man from Eretz Yisrael who owes a levirate marriage, and Rabbi Hanina
01.event: The man asks Rabbi Hanina whether he may travel to Babylonia to perform levirate marriage with his brother's widow.
01.turn: Rabbi Hanina answers with scorn about the dead brother, who married a Samaritan woman outside the land.
01.outcome: Rabbi Hanina implies the man should not follow his brother out of Eretz Yisrael; he is not permitted to go.
01.summary: A man whose brother died childless asked Rabbi Hanina if he could go down to Babylonia to marry the widow. Rabbi Hanina answered that the brother had married a foreign woman and died, and said blessed be God who killed him. He then asked if the man really wanted to follow him there, which meant he should stay.

02.actor: A Roman and a woman he wanted to marry
02.event: A Roman asked a woman to marry him, she refused, and he ate peeled pomegranates in front of her until she fell ill from the saliva she swallowed.
02.turn: He offered to cure her if she would marry him, and she agreed.
02.outcome: He ate pomegranates again and had her spit out the saliva until a green leaf-like thing came out, and she was cured.
02.summary: A Roman asked a woman to marry him and she said no. He peeled and ate pomegranates in front of her, and she swallowed her saliva until she became ill. He then offered a cure in exchange for marriage, had her spit out the saliva while he ate again, and she recovered.

03.actor: A man who deposited sesame plants with his friend
03.event: The owner asked for his sesame back and the keeper said he had already taken it; the owner said the amount and barrel prove otherwise, and the keeper said those were different sesame.
03.turn: The depositor offers a proof (the amount, the barrel) and the keeper counters that these are other plants.
03.outcome: The case went before the Sages, but the verdict is not given in the passage and the surrounding text only gives opinions about it.
03.summary: A man deposited sesame plants with a friend and later asked for them back. The friend said he had already taken them. The owner pointed to the amount and the barrel, but the friend said those were other plants. The case went before the Sages.
03.missing: The ruling or final resolution of the dispute.

04.actor: Bar Shatya and the witnesses, with Rav Ashi ruling
04.event: Bar Shatya, who was sometimes insane, sold land, and two witnesses said he sold when sane while two others said he sold when insane.
04.turn: The testimonies contradicted and cancelled each other.
04.outcome: Rav Ashi ruled the two cancel out, so the land remains in Bar Shatya's possession.
04.summary: Bar Shatya, a man who periodically went insane, sold property. Two witnesses said he was sane at the sale and two said he was insane. Rav Ashi ruled that the pairs cancel each other, so the land stays with Bar Shatya. It is cited as a precedent for a legal argument.
04.missing: It is a brief precedent used for argument; the story's own setting and details are minimal.

05.actor: The sister of Rami bar Hama and her husband Rav Avya
05.event: The wife's marriage contract was lost and the couple came to Rav Yosef to ask what to do.
05.turn: Rav Yosef cited Rabbi Meir's strict view, the Rabbis' lenient view, and Abaye pointed out that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees.
05.outcome: Rav Yosef told them to go and write her a new marriage contract.
05.summary: Rami bar Hama's sister was married to Rav Avya, and her marriage contract was lost. They asked Rav Yosef, who first cited the dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages about living without a contract. When Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir, Rav Yosef said that in that case, go and write her a new one.

06.event: Rabbi was about to rule according to the Rabbis (that a court's mistaken sale is void), and Perata asked what advantage then remained to the court's power.
06.outcome: In Rav Dimi's version Rabbi reversed his ruling; in Rav Safra's version Rabbi never carried it out.
06.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi acted, or was about to act, in accordance with the Rabbis in a case. Perata, grandson of Rabbi Perata the Great, asked what advantage the court's power would have if so. Rabbi then reversed his ruling, or in the other version did not carry it out.

07.actor: A debtor who claimed his money belonged to a gentile, and the Sages
07.event: Rav Hama explains the incident behind a ruling: a debtor with money and land had attached his money to a gentile.
07.turn: The debtor acted improperly in hiding his money.
07.outcome: The Sages acted improperly with him by forcing him to sell his land.
07.summary: Rav Pappa asked Rav Hama what actually happened in the incident behind a ruling attributed to Rava. Rav Hama said the debtor had money but claimed it belonged to a gentile. Since he acted improperly, the Sages treated him improperly and made him sell his land to pay.
07.missing: The creditor's side and the actual court proceedings are not narrated; only a compressed explanation.

08.event: Rav Hisda's daughter asked him whether he did not wish to sleep a little after his nights of study.
08.turn: He answered that long days of death are coming in which he will sleep a lot.
08.outcome: No action follows; the exchange ends with his reply.
08.summary: Rav Hisda's daughter asked if he did not want to sleep a little. He replied that days that are long but short for study and mitzvot are coming soon, and then we will sleep a lot.
08.missing: It is a short exchange with no event beyond the dialogue.

10.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, then Rabbi Hiyya
10.event: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi visited Gavla, saw grape clusters as large as calves, and lamented that the earth gave its fruit to gentiles.
10.outcome: The next year Rabbi Hiyya saw clusters only as big as goats and the locals told him not to do what his colleague did.
10.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Gavla and saw clusters of grapes as big as calves. He cried out to the earth, asking why it produced fruit for gentiles who ruled over them because of their sins. The next year Rabbi Hiyya came and saw clusters the size of goats, and the locals told him not to do to them what his colleague had done.

11.event: In a year of famine the Sages asked Rav Yosef to pray for mercy.
11.turn: Rav Yosef refused, arguing that Elisha, who supported 2,200 scholars, did not pray in a time of anger.
11.outcome: He did not pray; the passage ends on his rhetorical question.
11.summary: During years of divine anger and hunger, the Sages asked Rav Yosef to pray for mercy. He replied that Elisha, who supported 2,200 scholars, did not pray at such times, so why should he.
11.missing: No further outcome (whether the famine ended) is given.

12.actor: Rabbi Elai, Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi, and Rabbi Shimon bar Abba
12.event: Two scholars sitting and studying stood up when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed by.
12.turn: He told them they need not stand, because they were ordained scholars and he only an associate, and because the Torah they were studying does not stand for its students.
12.outcome: He released them from standing; no later action is told.
12.summary: Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi were studying when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed, and they stood for him. He told them they did not need to, since they were ordained and he was not, and since one does not stand for a scholar during Torah study.
12.missing: It is a brief anecdote used to illustrate a ruling.

13.event: Rav Aha found his son not sharp after studying with Abaye and went to study himself; Abaye arranged that he would have to sleep in a study hall haunted by a demon.
13.turn: The demon appeared as a seven-headed serpent and Rav Aha bowed in prayer, each bow knocking off a head.
13.outcome: The demon died; the next day Rav Aha told the townspeople they would have endangered him had no miracle occurred.
13.summary: Rav Aha bar Yaakov sent his son to Abaye, but the son returned not sharp, so Aha decided to go and study himself. Abaye, hearing he was coming, told the town not to give him lodging, hoping a miracle would kill a demon that harmed those in the study hall. Aha slept there, the demon appeared as a seven-headed serpent, and with every bow of his prayer a head fell off. In the morning he said that without a miracle they would have put him in danger.

15.event: A man with much movable property wished to give it as a gift and was told he could only do so by transferring it through land.
15.turn: He bought a plot of land near Jerusalem and declared the northern part given to a named person together with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.
15.outcome: He died and the Sages upheld his words.
15.summary: A Madonite in Jerusalem had a lot of movable property and wanted to give it away as a gift. The Sages said he could only do so by transferring it together with land. He bought a plot near Jerusalem and said the northern part was for so-and-so, with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels. He died and the Sages carried out his words.

16.event: Orphans' movable property was held by Rabbi Banai and the daughters came before Shmuel.
16.turn: Shmuel ordered Rabbi Banai to sustain them.
16.outcome: Shmuel's instruction is the end; it is used as a proof for a legal question.
16.summary: Rabbi Banai held movable property belonging to orphans. The orphan daughters came before Shmuel, who told Rabbi Banai to go and sustain them.
16.missing: Why they came, and what happened after, are not told; it is cited as legal evidence.

18.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
18.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a halakha attributed to him.
18.turn: Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it, citing Rami bar Abba in Rav Huna's name, and the three lessons Rav Yosef had drawn from it.
18.outcome: The reminder shows the halakha was his own teaching; Rav Yosef's forgetting is explained by illness.
18.summary: Rav Yosef said he did not hear this teaching from his teachers. His student Abaye replied that he himself had told them this teaching, and quoted the statement of Rami bar Abba in Rav Huna's name and the three lessons Rav Yosef had drawn from it. The text explains Rav Yosef had forgotten his learning after an illness.
18.missing: Rav Yosef's own response to the reminder is not given.

19.actor: Reish Lakish, judges, and Rabbi Yohanan
19.event: Judges ruled according to Rabbi Tarfon and Reish Lakish reversed their ruling.
19.turn: Rabbi Yohanan criticized Reish Lakish for treating it like a Torah-law error.
19.outcome: The incident ends with Rabbi Yohanan's rebuke; the Gemara then analyses the disagreement.
19.summary: Some judges ruled a case according to Rabbi Tarfon, and Reish Lakish reversed their action. Rabbi Yohanan told him that he had acted as if this were a matter of Torah law.
